ideas.title: The drawing bench: my beak hauls the wire through stone
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: Strong because the player's pull speed meets a solved load that pushes back through Lumi's body, so nobody is just watching a lone object, and the neck is a defect you made yourself and carry forward. The risk is a one-plate, one-rod rig with a scripted lean. If the film shows a wire getting longer with no visible haul, it falls straight back into the island's tired film of a simulated object left alone.

ideas.title: The hot wire droops before it parts
ideas.critique: The payoff, a copper wire that glows hottest and parts, was the last-but-ten post, and an 8 mm sag only adds a small refinement to it. The real expansion law is honest, but what someone watching sees is the same lone failing wire under a fixed camera.

ideas.title: A needle that tells me the current
ideas.critique: A needle swinging in a bowl of water is already on the island. Reading the current from a solved wire is the real step, but it will show as the same damped swing. Its worth is as an instrument the road will use, not as something new to watch.

ideas.title: My motor hums its speed
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: This is the one form here the last ten posts don't have: sound made from the solve, with ripple, commutation steps and brush bounce, heard live and not only filmed. The weak spot is the motor itself: it barely turned in its own post. A hum from a rotor that stalls is a short, sad sound, and a few hand-picked board modes would make it a rig.

ideas.title: Cells in clam shells
ideas.critique: A real road step: gathering and stacking power is play, and polarisation that recovers with rest is a nice touch. But the pitched payoff, a wire going from dull to orange, is the glowing-wire picture again. Four clams in a row is also a prop arrangement unless the plate area and gap really come from what the player built.

ideas.title: Green rock to a copper bead
ideas.critique: Pumping a fire hot enough is a skill worth having, and it turns the kiln into a smelter. The chemistry as pitched is temperature thresholds that switch states, and a bead 'found in the ash' hides the one moment worth seeing.

ideas.title: A wheel on the dune
ideas.critique: Ruts in the terrain and Bekker sinkage are new ways the ground answers, and the wheels become the cart's legs. But 'two wheels let go side by side, different outcomes' is the island's most worn recipe exactly, and the snowball already left a stripe going downhill.

ideas.title: The cart's first fuse
ideas.critique: Stall current with no back-EMF is a real lesson, but it rests on a cart and a motor that runs, and neither exists yet. Made now, it is a thin wire glowing and parting once more.

ideas.title: Lumi's beak that grips
ideas.critique: A general grip with the head and neck carrying the load serves every bench and finally puts the player's own hands into the building, which is the strongest play here. Picking up a nail is a modest picture. It lives or dies on whether the weight really shows in the body, rather than a head that tracks to the grip point.

ideas.title: A night of glowing wires
ideas.critique: Lamps as real Planck emitters in the traced scene play to the path tracer, but a glowing hot thing lighting the sand at night has been posted already. The thin-or-thick trade-off is the only play, and gathering friends to the light risks being a scripted scene.
